THIS APPEAL COMING ON FOR ORDERS, THIS DAY,
JUDGMENT WAS DELIVERED THEREIN AS UNDER:
CORAM: HON'BLE MRS JUSTICE P SREE SUDHA  ORAL JUDGMENT Heard the arguments of both sides.

2. This appeal is filed against the judgment and award of the Tribunal passed in MVC No.1054/2019 dated 05.12.2022 by the Court of II Additional Senior Civil Judge and MACT, Vijayapura (for short 'the Tribunal')
3.

entities.text: II Additional Senior Civil Judge and MACT, Vijayapura
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Injured claimant aged 22 years met with an accident on 15.09.2020 and filed a claim petition claiming compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- with interest at the rate of 18% per annum.
The Tribunal considering entire material on record, granted an amount of Rs.3,44,016/- with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till realization/deposit.
NC: 2025:KHC-K:7424 HC-KAR 4.

Aggrieved by the said order, this appeal is preferred in which it is contended that, he spent Rs.2,00,000/- for medical expenses marked at Ex.P8 and P9, but the Tribunal granted Rs.68,116/-
and meager amounts are granted under other heads.

PW2 - Doctor assessed the disability as 20 to 25% to the left lower limb and he mentioned the range of left knee and ankle terminally restricted and painful; on palpation mild tenderness over the operated site, X-ray of left knee discloses old healed fracture of left tibia with implant in situ, there is mild to moderate wasting of left leg muscles compared to right side, constitution 3% disability, there is loss of range of movement of left knee and ankle.

It is further contended that the Tribunal has taken the income as 13,750/- and thus,
requested for enhancement of compensation and also to enhance the interest to 9%.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned counsel for respondent No.2 has contended that, PW2 is not a treated doctor and the fractures are united as per cross examination of PW2.
She further stated that restriction of the movement can be normalized if he takes physiotherapy in due course of time.
NC: 2025:KHC-K:7424 HC-KAR 6.

As per Ex.P5 - wound certificate, appellant sustained following injuries:-
 i) Abrasion 2x3 cm over right hand  ii) Laceration 2x1x0.5 cm over right foot.
iii) Laceration 10x6x1 cm over left leg.
iv) Fracture shaft of left tibia (as per X-ray)
Out of the above said injuries, 1, 2 and 3 are simple and injury No.4 is grievous in nature and PW2 issued disability certificate assessed the same as 20 to 22%.
In the accident to the left leg, it was observed that, fracture noted at mid shaft of tibia with IM nail and screw fixation.
Ex.P10 is the disability certificate.

The Tribunal considered 1/3rd of 22% i.e.,
7% and this Court after considering the fact that it is a united fracture, finds it reasonable to confirm the disability assessed by the Tribunal.
Hence, the disability assessed by the Tribunal is hereby confirmed and it needs no interference.

7. The Tribunal has rightly taken the appellant's notional income as Rs.13,750/-, as met with an accident in the year 2020 and he was aged 23 years and appropriately taken NC: 2025:KHC-K:7424 HC-KAR the multiplier as '18'.
Accordingly, the loss of future earning capacity calculated as Rs.2,07,900/- by the Tribunal needs no interference and hereby it is confirmed.
8. The Tribunal granted Rs.68,116/- towards medical expenses and it is hereby confirmed and it needs no interference.

9. As per Ex.P7 - discharge summary, he was hospitalized from 15.09.2020 to 21.09.2020 i.e., for 6 days, therefore, this Court finds it reasonable to grant an amount of Rs.50,000/- for pain and suffering, Rs.25,000/- for loss of amenities, Rs.30,000/- for transportation, extra nourishment and attendant charges.

10. He might not have attended any other work at least for a period of 4 months, therefore,
Rs.55,000/- (13,750x4) is awarded under the head - loss of income during laid up period and this Court also finds it is required to grant an amount of Rs.30,000/- for removal of the implants.

NC: 2025:KHC-K:7424 HC-KAR Mohammed Mohaseen vs Tammanna And Anr on 3 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/197795273/
3 11.

sentences.text: In all, the total compensation is Rs.4,66,016/- with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till realization.

12. The award passed by the Tribunal is modified as under:
 Heads Amount in Rs.
 1. Loss of income 2,07,900/-
 2. Pain and suffering 50,000/-
 3. Loss of amenities 25,000/-
 4.

Medical expenses 68,116/-
 5. Attendant, diet, conveyance and 30,000/-
 other charges

6 . Loss of earning during laid up 55,000/-
 period for 4 months  7. Removal of the implants 30,000/-
 Total 4,66,016/-
Respondent No.2 - Insurance Company has already deposited the amount awarded by the Tribunal.

Thus, the appellant is entitled for enhanced compensation of Rs.1,22,000/- with interest at the rate of 6%.
13.

In the result, the following order is passed:
(i) Appeal is allowed in part.
NC: 2025:KHC-K:7424 HC-KAR (ii) The appellant is entitled for enhanced compensation of Rs.1,22,000/- with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till realization.
However, as per order dated 13.02.2025, the appellant is not entitled for interest for the delayed period of 573 days in filing the appeal.
(iii) Respondent No.2-Insurance Company is  directed to deposit the aforesaid compensation amount within one month from the date of this judgment.
(iv) On such deposit, appellant is permitted to withdraw the entire amount along with interest accrued on it.
